title: Weight-only INT8 (GPTQ/AWQ) adaptive calibration & regression harness
creator: Marco Nguyen
description:
Background: We need a robust, automated harness to validate INT8 weight-only quantization profiles produced by GPTQ and AWQ pipelines. Previous tickets focused on profile generation and basic regtests; this ticket builds an adaptive calibration + regression test runner that mirrors production inference patterns (short/long sequences, tail-token sensitivity, multibatch traffic) and integrates canary orchestration for safe rollouts.

Scope: implement an end-to-end test harness that (1) runs per-model GPTQ and AWQ profiles through calibration pipelines, (2) measures accuracy regressions on a curated prompt corpus and golden evals, (3) exercises canary routing and rollback triggers in Redwood Console, and (4) publishes metrics and alerts for nightly runs. The harness should be usable in CI (smoke) and as a nightly long-run.

Out of scope: retraining or modifying model weights; full-scale perf benchmarking for every hardware SKU (we will sample representative instances).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can execute GPTQ and AWQ weight-only profiles for at least 5 representative models (e.g., small/med/large families) in CI smoke mode
Golden-eval accuracy degradation <= 0.8% relative delta (top-1/ROUGE/EM as applicable) for each model/profile combination; deviations logged with prompt-level diffs
Latency and throughput regression per-profile documented; any profile that increases median token latency by >10% must be flagged
Canary orchestration configured: harness can register canary release metadata to Console, run traffic split simulation, and trigger automated rollback if accuracy SLOs breached
Nightly job artifacts (calibration logs, per-layer thresholds, token tail sensitivity plots) stored to artifacts bucket and linked in the run summary
Dashboards and alerts: a console dashboard exists for regtest runs and an alert rule fires on accuracy regressions or stability failures
implementation_notes: Reuse the existing quant-profile CI runner but extend pipeline to run an adaptive calibration stage that sweeps per-layer scale-factors and collects KV-cache interaction metrics
Introduce a deterministic seeding mode for GPTQ/AWQ calibration to make regression comparisons stable across runs
Instrument the harness to record token-by-token deltas and prefix-sensitivity; store diffs in ndjson for downstream analysis
Add lightweight mock routing for canary simulation (no real traffic change in hosted) and integrate with Console rollout API to create a canary object
Provide an opt-in production shadow mode for burst tests that mirrors small fractions of live traffic to a private bucket (requires product sign-off)
test_steps: 1) Checkout harness branch and ensure CI runner has access to model-artifacts bucket
3) Validate generated calibration artifacts appear in artifacts/<run-id>/calibration/ and per-layer thresholds present
5) Confirm metrics uploaded to Console test-dashboard and that canary object was created with expected metadata
6) Simulate accuracy breach by toggling baseline comparator and confirm alert/rollback logic triggers
monitoring_and_telemetry: Collect: top-1/top-5 accuracy, perplexity, ROUGE where applicable, median token latency, 95p latency, tail-token KL/divergence
Expose: per-layer scale histograms, calibration loss curves, weight-quantization error distribution
Alert rules: accuracy-delta > 0.8% for >3 runs, median-latency increase >10% vs baseline, harness failed run rate >5% over 24h
rollout_and_rollback_plan: Create canary release via Console API with 1% synthetic traffic for 1 hour, then 5% for 3 hours if stable
Rollback triggers: accuracy delta breach OR latency breach or harness failure; rollback executed by automation that reverts to last-good profile and notifies owners
Manual override: SRE/Model-Ops can pause canary and require a manual triage run
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: stochastic calibration noise causes false positives. Mitigation: deterministic seeding + ensemble median across 3 calibration seeds
Risk: calibration runtime is long for large models. Mitigation: smoke/nightly modes and early-stopping heuristics based on calibration loss plateau
Risk: perf regressions on certain hardware. Mitigation: sample representative instance types and tag profiles with recommended hardware
